jobs.occupation: Business Consultant – East Africa
jobs.description:
Business Consultant – East Africa

Employer: Adamcon ApS, CVR 33608989
Contact: Adam D.
Location: Copenhagen, Denmark, with travel to East Africa for regional events, forums and client work
Start date: 1 January 2027
Contract: 2 years, fixed-term, with the possibility of renewal
Salary: DKK 37,500 gross per month
Benefits: Statutory holiday pay under the Danish Holiday Act and ATP contributions as required by law
Application deadline: 31 October 2026

About Adamcon
Adamcon ApS is a Danish business consulting company expanding from Europe into East Africa. We are looking for a consultant who wants to help build that growth into lasting partnerships and measurable results.

The role
You will identify growth opportunities in the East African consulting market and build strong, lasting relationships with key stakeholders. You will provide strategic insight to guide the company’s direction, lead high-impact projects from concept to completion, and represent Adamcon ApS at regional events and forums.

What we are looking for

• 
Proven experience in business consulting in East Africa

• 
Strategic thinking and problem-solving skills

• 
Strong communication and negotiation skills

• 
Ability to deliver results in dynamic environments

• 
Fluency in English; knowledge of local languages is an advantage

Why this role
This is a chance to help shape a new market from the start. You will take projects from first idea to final delivery, build a regional network, and see your work create real value for partners in East Africa. We are looking for people who see opportunity where others see complexity, and who want to grow with the company.

Terms of employment
The contract may be renewed. It may also be terminated before the end of the term in accordance with the notice and termination provisions of the employment contract and Danish law.

Equal opportunities
Adamcon ApS welcomes applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability or background.

Right to work
Applicants must have the right to work in Denmark. Adamcon ApS does not sponsor work or residence permits.

How to apply
Send your CV and cover letter to You@adamcon.vip with the subject line: “Business Consultant – East Africa Application.”

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Materials for Power Electronics / Printed Electronics
jobs.description:
The cross-border region Denmark-Germany is a powerhouse in industrial electronics. The Centre for Industrial Electronics (CIE) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) was established by a strong partnership between industry, academia and regional authorities. CIE is located at the campus of SDU Sønderborg and surrounded by a vibrant industrial environment. CIE is part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the Faculty of Engineering.

 

Job description 

We are seeking an innovative and visionary Assistant Professor to join the Centre for Industrial Electronics in Sønderborg. The Centre currently has 40 staff, including full and associate professors, assistant professors, postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and support staff. Funding has been secured to support to establish new research and test laboratories in key areas of industrial electronics. Our ambition is to deliver excellence in research, innovation, and education.

It is our vision that the Centre for Industrial Electronics at SDU will excel in areas of key relevance for companies in the region of Southern Denmark and beyond. 

Candidates are thus required to have a proven research records at least one of the following fields:

• 
General power electronics and its reliability

• 
Multimaterial additive manufacturing

• 
Printed electronics

• 
Polymer composites and nanocomposites for energy applications

• 
Surface and interface engineering

• 
Dielectric materials and capacitor technology

• 
Materials for power electronics

• 
Energy-device manufacturing

• 
Sustainable and circular electronics

 

Qualifications

The candidates must have a PhD in Electrical Engineering/Materials science/Mechanical engineering, or a closely related discipline. 

We also expect:

• 
An outstanding research and publication track record 

• 
Experience with industrial collaboration

• 
Research experience in multi-material additive manufacturing of functional polymer composites

• 
Experience developing polymer nanocomposite dielectrics and thin-film capacitors

• 
Knowledge of nanoparticle surface modification, dispersion, and interface engineering

• 
Hands-on experience in materials processing, device fabrication, and electrical characterization

• 
Ability to investigate relationships between material structure, manufacturing conditions, and electrical performance

• 
Peer-reviewed publications in functional materials, additive manufacturing, or energy-device research

• 
Experience collaborating across materials science and electrical engineering.

Further desirable qualifications:

• 
Experience with bio-based, self-healing, or temperature-resistant capacitor materials

• 
Knowledge of scalable thin-film fabrication, including layer-by-layer deposition or coating.

• 
Experience translating research into industrial applications, particularly embedded heating, sensing, or battery-conditioning systems.

• 
Experience preparing research proposals, securing research resources, and training students.

 

Contact and further information

For information about the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical engineering, which encompasses SDU Electrical Engineering please see https://www.sdu.dk/en/ime.

For specific information on section and centre, please visit www.sdu.dk/ee and www.sdu.dk/cie. 

You are also welcome to contact the Head of the CIE, Professor Thomas Ebel (ebel@sdu.dk,  +45 93 50 72 05) for further information. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

A panel will assess the qualification of the candidate for the described post based on the submitted material. 

The application should include:

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Ideas for research and development activities.

• 
Account of significant contributions to innovation in Electrical Engineering and Industrial Engineering Electronics.

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position. 

• 
Summary and documentation of teaching experience, including account of experience in training students and outreach. You may attach a Teaching Portfolio. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation). 

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included. 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period, and the position is open from start of 2027.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

Employment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Student Assistant in our Control Center - night shift position
jobs.description:
Nordic RCC is looking for candidates with a technical background and interest in the role as operator in our control center – is this something for you?

Do you like working by firm and well-defined procedures, yet alert to interfere in the process when needed? Are you open-minded and enjoy working in a diverse and international team? And are you eager to be part of something new and meaningful?

The position will mainly cover the operator position during the shift from 21.00 PM- 07.15 AM during both weekdays, weekends and holiday periods. The shifts, of individually 10.25 hours length, are distributed throughout the operator team. The schedule is planned and updated 3 times a year, securing at least a planned period of 4 months into the future. You can expect an average of around 70-80 working hours per month.

You will be working alone in the office during the shifts, with an on-call colleague standby to assist in any technical matters if needed.

If you can say yes to the above, then you may be just the person we are looking for.

Join Nordic RCC, a fast-developing company determined to make a significant impact in the energy sector and to provide for a secure and efficient transition to the green, sustainable energy system.

Nordic RCC – supporting security of supply and the green transition

Nordic RCC provides calculations and recommendations to the four Nordic Electricity Transmission System Operators (TSOs), Energinet, Fingrid, Statnett and Svenska Kraftnät. The main aim of the services is to ensure transparency and help the TSOs with operational planning to ensure continued security of supply with an increase of renewables in the system. In short: We play a small but important part of enabling the green transition.

You will join a team of young, diverse, and enthusiastic colleagues of currently more than 20 nationalities, and at times work in virtual teams with expert colleagues from the Nordic TSOs and potentially from all of Europe.

We are not looking for a specific educational background, but an engineering or similar technical or data-scientific background is preferred.

Whether you are in your bachelor’s program, or master’s degree program, that is not critically important. What is more important is your profile as a whole and how you are assessed to fit within the Nordic RCC organization.   

Key responsibilities for the operator role will be:

• 
Participating in the 24/7 control center shift roster: mainly covering the night hours 21.00 - 07.15.

• 
The shift starts in the control center relieving a colleague operator from the evening shift. When time allows, and the processes for the evening have finalized successfully, you have an opportunity to enter an adjacent resting facility. During the shift, when alerted, your responsibility is to enter the control center within minutes, intervening in the operational challenge faced. Next morning at 07.00, the morning operator will relieve you from your shift responsibility.

• 
Become an expert in executing the services provided from the 24/7 Nordic RCC control center.

• 
Maintaining your qualifications and knowledge in the operator control systems, including through routinely joining parallel shift during office hours to train in all NRCC services under the guidance of operators.

• 
Interface to the Nordic TSOs control centers.  

• 
Cooperation with the TSOs securing the process of services.

• 
Trouble shooting and fixing challenges in the services together with NRCC IT support.

• 
KPI recording and reporting, weekly and monthly.

• 
Aid the back-office operators in small tasks, such as visit approval to the core room.

Additional tasks and involvement

Depending on the flexibility and the competence of the candidate, together with the department needs, there will be an opportunity to be involved in other areas of responsibility. This way one will get a better understanding of the NRCC in general and meet fellow NRCC colleagues during normal business hours.

Other working areas, depending on department needs, can be:

• 
Involvement in testing system updates and features to be introduced to the control center.

• 
Quality assurance and updating operational procedures.

• 
Quality assurance and data retrieval for operational reporting.

• 
Provide analytical insights on operational planning scenarios.

You are open-minded, international mindset and excellence at working within structured patterns, at the same time the ability to maneuver within a huge spectrum of corner cases quickly, reliably, and independently.

You are structured and can appreciate a fast-paced environment from time to time. On a personal level you are open-minded, team-oriented and take responsibility.

Nordic RCC is an international office, so fluency in spoken and written English is required as well as a motivation for working in an international environment.

You will join a diverse and enthusiastic team in our office at Copenhagen Towers, Ørestad. Nordic RCC is home to over twenty nationalities, with a healthy gender balance and a wide range of ages and backgrounds. We value curiosity, fellowship, respect, and transparency—and we hope you see yourself in these values. 

Your daily workplace will be in the NRCC control center at the office premises in Copenhagen Towers, Ørestad.

Application deadline and contact information

Please apply online as soon as possible (in English) and no later than November 15th 2026.

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system.  

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.   Nordic RCC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 

If you have any questions, please contact Kenneth Nielsen, Head of Service Operations, KEN@nordic-rcc.net

• Picking and packing

• Utilizing a scanner

jobs.employer_name: International Council for The Exploration Of The Sea
jobs.description:
We have an exciting opportunity for a service-minded IT student to join our team as a Student Assistant in Copenhagen.

About ICES

The International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES) is an intergovernmental organization which advances marine science and promotes sustainable use of the seas. Our Secretariat is located in central Copenhagen and consists of approximately 85 staff representing more than 30 nationalities.

We are a small, collaborative workplace with an international outlook and a strong focus on learning, innovation, and knowledge sharing.

Your role

As our new Student Assistant, you'll help support the day-to-day IT needs of colleagues across an international workplace. Working alongside four other members of the IT team, you'll gain practical experience with modern workplace technologies while helping ensure that staff can work securely and effectively both in the office and remotely.

Responsibilities
You will help with:

• 
IT support and troubleshooting

• 
Device setup and user administration

• 
Microsoft 365 services and workplace technology

• 
Meeting room and conferencing equipment

• 
IT improvements, documentation, and security activities

• 
Support cybersecurity and compliance activities, including CIS controls, using cloud and Microsoft 365 security solutions.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for a student who has completed at least 3 years of education within IT, computer science, business informatics, technical engineering, or a related field, and who is currently pursuing further studies.

You do not need to know everything already. We are more interested in your curiosity, motivation, and willingness to learn.

For this role, we expect you to have:

• 
A strong interest in IT support and workplace technology

• 
Good understanding of Windows and Microsoft 365

• 
Confidence troubleshooting common technical issues

• 
Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken

• 
A structured and detail-oriented approach to your work

• 
The ability to work independently while also being a strong team player

Experience with Microsoft 365 administration, cloud technologies, device management, cybersecurity, or scripting is an advantage, but not required.

Why join ICES?

At ICES, you'll do more than provide IT support. You'll gain practical experience with modern workplace technology, work closely with experienced colleagues, and help support an international community of staff and scientists. We offer flexible working hours to fit around your studies, along with plenty of opportunities to learn and develop your skills.

Terms of Appointment

This is a paid student role, and the working hours are 15 hours per week. This position will be established with an initial duration of 6 months, with a starting date as soon as possible (preferably January 2027).

Apply Now!

jobs.occupation: RE-ADVERTISEMENT - Senior Team Leader for Research Support at the SDU eScience Center for National Research Infrastructure
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Team Leader to lead the Research Support team at the SDU eScience Center. The team plays a central role in helping researchers, research groups, and institutions across Denmark leverage advanced computing, cloud, AI, and data services to accelerate scientific discovery and innovation.

As Senior Team Leader, you will combine scientific insight, technical understanding, and leadership skills to guide a highly skilled team of research support specialists. Working closely with researchers across all disciplines, you will help shape how next-generation digital infrastructure is adopted and utilized within Danish research.

The position offers a unique opportunity to influence both the strategic development of national research services and the day-to-day support provided to tens of thousands of researchers using the center's infrastructure and platforms.

We are looking for a collaborative and forward-looking team leader who is passionate about enabling excellent research through advanced digital technologies. The ideal candidate combines scientific and technical credibility with strong leadership skills and enjoys working at the intersection of research, technology, and service development.

Key responsibilities

• 
Lead and develop the Research Support team, including strategic planning, prioritization, and staff development as part of the management group for the eScience center.

• 
Ensure high-quality support and consultancy services for researchers and customers from the public and private sector using the center's computing, cloud, AI, and data platforms.

• 
Build strong relationships with researchers, departments, external customers, and research infrastructures across SDU and nationally.

• 
Identify emerging research and customers’ needs and contribute to the development of new services, tools, and support initiatives.

• 
Collaborate with the center's technical teams to ensure that infrastructure and services align with user requirements and scientific developments.

Required qualifications

• 
Relevant university degree at Master's level or higher in computer science, engineering, natural sciences, data science, computational science, or a related discipline.

• 
Demonstrated leadership experience, including responsibility for teams, projects, or complex research initiatives.

• 
Strong understanding of computational research, scientific computing, data-intensive research, AI, or digital research infrastructure.

• 
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills in both Danish and English.

• 
The ability to engage effectively with researchers, technical specialists, customers from the private and public sector.

• 
Proven ability to translate scientific and customers’ needs into practical solutions and service developments.

Desired qualifications

• 
At least 3 years of experience from a university, research organization, national research infrastructure, or technology-oriented organization, including experience leading projects, teams, or research support activities. 

• 
Familiarity with high-performance computing, cloud computing, AI platforms, research data management, or research software engineering.

• 
Experience developing research support services, training activities, or scientific user communities.

• 
Knowledge of the Danish or European research infrastructure landscape.

While the positions offer flexibility and the possibility of remote work, the candidate is expected to be on-site in Odense.

About the SDU eScience Center

The SDU eScience Center is a national center for advanced digital research infrastructure at the University of Southern Denmark. The center develops, operates, and continuously advances large-scale computing, cloud, data, and AI services that support research across all scientific disciplines.

As Denmark's leading provider of research cyberinfrastructure, the center plays a central role in the national ecosystem for research computing and digital services. Through close collaborations with Danish universities, public institutions, and international partners, the center helps researchers access the computational resources and digital platforms needed to address some of society's most complex scientific and technological challenges.

The center is the primary developer and operator of UCloud, Denmark's national research cloud, which provides researchers with seamless access to advanced computing resources, AI and machine learning environments, data-intensive workflows, and scientific applications. Today, the platform serves tens of thousands of users across the Danish research community and forms a key component of the national e-infrastructure landscape.

At the SDU eScience Center, we combine the mindset of a research environment with the professionalism of a modern technology organization. Our teams work at the intersection of cloud computing, high-performance computing, AI infrastructure, data management, software engineering, and digital platform development. We actively contribute to open-source technologies and collaborate closely with researchers to transform emerging technologies into robust services with national impact.

At our center, you will be joining a highly collaborative community where brilliant minds—from IT professionals and data specialists to world-class researchers—converge to drive research innovation. We don’t just maintain servers; we build the foundational digital platforms that empower researchers, students and innovators to solve global challenges. 

Condition of Employment

The starting date for the job is as soon as possible, and it will be agreed with the successful candidate. The appointment is for a full-time permanent position.

All inquiries are welcome. Please contact:

Prof. Director Claudio Pica

SDU eScience center

Dept. of Mathematics and Computer Science

University of Southern Denmark

email: pica@cp3.sdu.dk

Application deadline 28 October 2026.

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Application must include cover letter, CV and certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

We recommend that you read how to apply before you apply.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology conducts high-quality research across all radiological specialties and contributes significantly to the education and development of highly qualified staff for both clinical and academic work.

The unit values researchers with diverse professional backgrounds and has approximately 20 affiliated members, including a professor, associate professors, PhD students, adjunct professors and others.

 University of Copenhagen

   

  We are offering a PhD fellowship in Veterinary Virology commencing 1st of February 2027.

  Our group and research
 Forskningsgruppen udfører forskning og undervisning inden for områderne enzootiske og zoonotiske virusinfektioner hos dyr. Forskningen vil de kommende år fokuseres på influenza infektioner i dyr, med fokus på zoonotiske aspekter af svine influenza virus. Gruppen bestå pt af ca. 20 forskere, phd studerende, studentermedhjælpere og 2 andre labornater. Vi har altid meget travlt, men har et godt arbejdsmiljø med masser af humor, kageklub og fleksible arbejdsopgaver og hvor alle hjælper alle. 

  The research group for Veterinary and Zoonotic Virology consists of around 20 members and as the name states work on both veterinary and zootonic viruses with a main focus on swine influenza A virus. We utilize different molecular methods such viral isolation in cells, qPCR/PCR, sequencing, ELISA and different immunological assays. The research group is very social and we have journal club, cake and breakfast club and Friday bars etc. 

  Project description
 The PhD project will be on cross-reactive vaccines for swine influenza A virus. The first part of the project will be focussed on establishing immunological assays in the laboratory and generating hyperimmune serum in pigs experimentally for following antigenic characterization of Danish swine influenza A virus. The second part of the PhD will be on selecting representative vaccine strains testing them first experimentally in pigs and afterwards in the field.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception. The position is available for up to 36 months and is part of a project led by Dr. Gregory Scott Francis that is supported by the SDU Department of Psychology. The starting date is March 15, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Research environment

The postdoc will be affiliated with the Research Unit of Health and Cognitive Psychology. The position is at the SDU Esbjerg campus but will also involve interaction with staff at the SDU Odense campus. 

Project description

A basic process of the visual system is to monitor the location and characteristics of objects in a scene, and the multiple object tracking (MOT) paradigm has identified many fundamental aspects of this process. With a rich literature of empirical results, this paradigm is ready for theoretical development, which this project intends to pursue using an integrate-and-fire neural network model known as LAMINART. A key aspect of the model is the ability to select/segment visual objects, which may explain how people can (seemingly) effortlessly track multiple objects in a dynamic visual scene. 

The successful candidate will be required to design, program and analyze an integrate-and-fire neural network model of visual perception. Good programming (Python) skills are required along with a good understanding of empirical methods and ways to connect empirical findings with model behavior. The position also involves teaching duties.

The project involves collaboration with Prof. Søren Krogh Andersen, also at SDU.

Qualifications

Ideally, applicants for the position should satisfy the following requirements:

• 
PhD level in psychology, cognitive (neuro)science, vision science, or a related field

• 
Research experience as evidenced by conference contributions and peer-reviewed journal articles in a field related to the offered position

• 
Expertise in visual attention and perception

• 
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to design, implement, and analyze complex experiments

• 
Be willing and able to teach for the Department of Psychology

• 
Prior experience with neural network modeling is a plus

• 
Prior experience with cognitive modelling is a plus

• 
Good command of statistics

• 
Good command of Python (or similar programming languages and a willingness to learn)

• 
Very good command of the English language in spoken and written form

• 
Some knowledge of the Danish language is a plus

Candidates who are about to obtain these qualifications are also encouraged to apply. 

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Greg Francis, SDU (email: gfrancis@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 16 98), or Professor Søren Krogh Andersen (email: skandersen@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 49 57)

Application deadline

The application deadline is November 08, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. CET.

Salary and terms of employment

The base salary for a postdoctoral researcher is DKK 36,877.42, with an additional job structure supplement of DKK 5,230.75. This brings the total monthly salary to DKK 42,108.16.

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in environmental medicine
jobs.description:
The translational pharmacology research group at Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine (CPPEM), Department of Public Health, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a fully funded 18 months postdoctoral position. The position is to be filled from January 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

About the Research Environment

The research areas of CPPEM span from pharmacoepidemiology to clinical studies, and cell-based basic pharmacology and environmental medicine. Collectively, CPPEM has a strong background in exposure to environmental chemicals, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetics, drug-drug interactions, and therapeutic drug monitoring. Specifically, the translational pharmacology group aims to understand variability in drug toxicity, drug metabolism and drug transport. Examples of this include cell-based models such as induced-pluripotent stem cells, primary human hepatocytes, and clinical studies. The pharmacoepidemiological research group utilizes the world-class Danish registries as well as international data sources to assess pharmacological questions in large populations. The environmental medicine group studies the impact of early life exposures to environmental chemicals. In particular PFAS is a focus area, with studies of the adverse health effects of exposure, biomonitoring and advising national and international authorities. The analytical chemistry laboratory analyzes concentrations of drugs or environmental chemicals in various matrices. 

In the Environmental Medicine group we are looking for a post doc funded by Novo Nordic Foundation and ERC advanced grant. The projects focus on the Odense Child Cohort and study the impact of early life exposures to environmental chemicals. Especially PFAS and their adverse effects on maternal and child health (e.g. the brain, immune, metabolic and reproductive system). In addition, we aim to identify toxicity of short PFAS including trifluoroacetic acid, widely used but considered less toxic due to their short half-life. 

We are seeking a candidate with a PhD in medicine, pharmacology, public health, or a related discipline. Work within environmental medicine is an advance, and epidemiological and statistical skills are essential. Motivation, curiosity, and a strong drive to excel in environmental research are very important. Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English is a requirement. The position includes independent scientific writing, clinical project leading, and supervision of students. You should be interested in contributing both to the scientific armamentarium in our department and to our collegial culture. It is also expected that the post doc contributes to additional fundraising for the projects as well as research collaborations and the continuation of the Odense Child Cohort, and takes on teaching responsibilities within the department. You will, in your daily work, refer to Professor Tina Kold Jensen, but also engage in a very active collaboration with the full research group.

Your qualifications

• 
PhD in medicine, pharmacology, public health, or a related discipline.

•

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
jobs.description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

• 
A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

• 
Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

• 
Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

• 
The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

• 
Good written and spoken English. 

• 
A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

• 
Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

• 
Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

• 
Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

• 
Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

• 
International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

• 
Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

• 
Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

• 
Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

• 
Two letters of recommendation. 

• 
A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

• 
The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

• 
Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Further information about the scientific content of the position is available from:

Wu Chen
Associate Professor
Department of Green Technology
SDU Life Cycle Engineering
University of Southern Denmark

jobs.occupation: OT Security Architect - Renewables, Location: Denmark , DK - Esbjerg, DK - Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced and motivated OT Security Architect and do you want to leave your mark on the global energy industry? If so, we want to hear from you! 
 
Your position
 
In your new position as OT Security Architect in the Renewables division, you will be a valuable member of the OT Security Team, whose mission is to ensure excellent OT security deliveries on large-scale EPC substation projects. You will have the chance to take the architectural lead and help shape a collaborative team culture built on expertise and knowledge-sharing. Above all, your work will make a real difference to the global energy sector.

Your place of work will be at one of our offices in either Esbjerg or Copenhagen. The position is full-time, and you can expect to travel 10–30 days per year.

“Every day, we help enable the green energy transition by building secure, resilient OT solutions that ensure renewable energy assets operate safely and reliably.” - OT Security Architect & Team Lead, Reza Sarafrazjoo.
 
Your tasks & responsibilities 

In our Renewables division, we have major EPC projects in the pipeline for both short- and long-term operations. As an OT Security Architect, you will take the architectural lead and support all OT Security areas across the EPC substation projects.

Your tasks will include but are not limited to:

• Contributing to the implementation of industry-accepted good practice and required Cyber/OT Security architecture at solution level, typically based on standards such as IEC 62443, ISO 27001, and NIS
• Helping define products and standards relevant to OT Security and infrastructure
• Hands-on experience with cybersecurity audits and compliance frameworks, including ISO 27001, Critical Infrastructure regulations, and IEC 62443
• Reviewing requirements/ITT packages and providing input to tenders consisting of calculations, solutions, descriptions, clarifications, and reservations
• Taking on an advisory or active role in infrastructure, identity access management, or logging/event-based activities
• Being responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing FAT, SAT, and SIT activities to ensure successful system delivery and integration
• Implementing customer-specific Cyber/OT Security requirements in substation design for multiple systems and subsystems, such as SCADA, low-voltage, HVAC, Auxiliary Control and Monitoring System, etc.

Crucial to this position is your ability to take ownership of project deliverables and coordinate OT Security deadlines with internal and external stakeholders. You should thrive in a leading role where your skills, collaboration, and structured approach help ensure that requirements are met.
 
Your profile & qualifications

You are a team player who enjoys leading projects and working with stakeholders to align on timing, scope, and objectives. You know when technical expertise should be brought in to support delivery. To us, this means that you have a structured and solution-oriented approach, the ability to influence stakeholders, and the dedication to see tasks through to completion.

You will be part of a team of six colleagues that values quality, attention to detail, and a flexible working environment. We are sociable, helpful, and open to input, and we work in a dedicated, structured, and execution-focused way while respecting the agility that is a natural part of our core tasks. We want the same from you.

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have:

• A minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in OT Security from a similar position
• A Tech Lead mentality – we are not seeking an extreme subject matter expert, but a well-rounded colleague who can work through heavily structured large projects involving many stakeholders 
• The ability to know when additional technical specialists or resources are needed to complete a project
• Excellent communication skills and fluency in English
• Experience working in complex engineering projects, as well as project and stakeholder management, is an advantage

If you have any questions, you are more than welcome to contact OT Security Architect & Team Lead, Reza Sarafrazjoo.
 
Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey: how to get there. We provide the answers needed to make change real, because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do, and this is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.
So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

jobs.occupation: Data engineer for analytics platform with BI expertise and an interest in the green energy transition
jobs.description:

Are you a data engineer who is curious, open‑minded, and initiative-taking — someone who enjoys working in an explorative and collaborative environment? Do you want to collaborate with engineers, application developers, and data scientists to unlock insights from the vast amounts of data behind our services? 

We are looking for a Data Engineer with BI expertise to join our Data and Analytics team at Nordic RCC. Nordic RCC – supporting security of supply and the green energy transition 

Nordic Regional Coordination Centre (RCC) provides critical services and insights to support the national Transmission System Operators (TSOs) in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark — to ensure the efficient operation and use of the Nordic power system and high security of power supply at any time. 

Based in Copenhagen, Nordic RCC is one of six RCCs in Europe, equally owned by the Nordic region's four electricity TSOs: Fingrid, Statnett, Svenska Kraftnät, and Energinet. 

As European power systems integrate and evolve to meet climate goals, Nordic RCC provides regional coordination, integrated services, regional insights and recommendations to the Nordic TSOs and their control centres, to support cross-border operational security 24/7.

Right now, we are looking for a Data Engineer who likes to make a difference!

The Data and Analytics team consists of 10 employees and consultants and plays a central role in enabling data-driven decision-making across Nordic RCC. The team develops and maintains data pipelines, analytics products, BI solutions, platform services, and information services that support operational, strategic, and regulatory needs. 

As a Data Engineer with BI expertise, you will help design, build, operate, and improve our analytics platform and the data products built on it. You will work closely with data scientists, engineers, developers, infrastructure teams, external providers, and stakeholders to deliver reliable data pipelines, intuitive BI solutions, and user-friendly data services. 

Your work will directly influence how Nordic RCC uses data to improve processes, services, and operational decision-making. Your key responsibilities will include: 

• 
Design, build, and optimize scalable data pipelines, data models, integrations, and curated datasets. 

• 
Develop BI dashboards, reports, and data products that turn complex data into clear insights. 

• 
Operate and improve analytics platform services, including data platforms, BI solutions, JupyterHub, user-facing analytics environments, and supporting applications. 

• 
Ensure data quality, reliability, monitoring, and operational visibility across pipelines, BI products, and platform services. 

• 
Monitor and optimize platform performance, resource use, computer storage, and analytical workloads. 

• 
Collaborate with data scientists, engineers, developers, infrastructure teams, external providers, and stakeholders to deliver production-ready analytics solutions. 

• 
Support the development of platform architecture, metadata, governance practices, and service-oriented delivery models such as Data-as-a-Service and Platform-as-a-Service. 

• 
Document data flows, platform components, operational procedures, and technical solutions to support maintainability and knowledge sharing. 

We are looking for someone with several of the following qualifications: 

• 
Minimum 5 years of experience as a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, BI Developer, Platform Engineer, Application Developer, or similar. 

• 
Strong experience with ETL/ELT pipelines, modern data architectures, SQL, and data warehousing concepts. 

• 
Hands-on experience with BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, or similar. 

• 
Experience operating and optimizing analytics platforms in production environments. 

• 
Experience with cloud-native technologies and analytics platforms such as Microsoft Azure, Databricks, Azure Synapse, Snowflake, or similar. 

• 
Familiarity with orchestration, monitoring, DevOps, CI/CD, Python, containerization, Kubernetes, storage solutions, or data platform infrastructure 

• 
Experience operationalizing analytics models, enabling data consumption, or supporting service-oriented delivery models is an advantage. 

• 
Knowledge of power systems and the energy sector is a plus, but not a requirement. 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet all the listed requirements. Your experience and perspective could be exactly what we are looking for. 

Working Environment 

You will join a diverse and enthusiastic team in our office at Copenhagen Towers, Ørestad. Nordic RCC is home to over twenty nationalities, with a healthy gender balance and a wide range of ages and backgrounds. We value curiosity, fellowship, respect, and transparency—and we hope you see yourself in these values. 

We offer flexible work arrangements to support a healthy work-life balance, including the option to work from home part of the time. Due to the collaborative nature of our work, physical presence in the office is expected on most days. 

You’ll report to Data & Analytics team-lead and collaborate regularly with colleagues from the Nordic RCC and occasionally also from the Nordic TSOs. Travel is limited and will not exceed 15 days per year. 

Nordic RCC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 

Application & Security Clearance 

Please apply online in English no later than 5 November 2026. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis. 

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.   

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system.  

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.   Nordic RCC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.occupation: Produktionskoordinator & Creative Specialist – barselsvikariat / Production Coordinator & Creative Specialist (Maternity Cover)
jobs.description:
Hos AVdesign i Billund søger vi en erfaren produktionskoordinator til et barselsvikariat i vores videoteam.

Du skal være god til at planlægge, holde overblik og få produktionerne til at hænge sammen – også når der kommer ændringer undervejs. Du får tæt kontakt med vores kunder og kolleger og deltager både i koordineringen og de praktiske opgaver i studiet og på location.

Om jobbet

Du får en central rolle i planlægningen og gennemførelsen af vores produktioner. Vi arbejder med video, livestreaming, produktoptagelser i studiet og andre medieproduktioner. Opgaverne varierer, og du skal have lyst til at hjælpe til, hvor der er brug for dig.

Vi søger dig, der har erfaring som producer, produktionsleder eller koordinator og er vant til at holde styr på planer, mennesker og deadlines.

Dine opgaver bliver blandt andet at:

• 
Planlægge og koordinere produktioner i samarbejde med teamet.

• 
Holde styr på tidsplaner, logistik og praktiske aftaler.

• 
Have løbende kontakt med kunder og samarbejdspartnere og sikre, at de er godt informeret undervejs.

• 
Deltage i produktionerne og hjælpe med praktiske og kreative opgaver.

• 
Følge op på opgaver og sørge for, at projekterne bliver leveret til tiden.

• 
Håndtere ændringer og finde løsninger, når noget ikke går som planlagt.

Du bliver en del af et team, hvor vi hjælper hinanden og deler viden, idéer og erfaringer.

Om dig

Du arbejder struktureret, tager initiativ og følger dine opgaver til dørs. Du er god til at kommunikere med både kunder og kolleger og kan bevare overblikket, når flere opgaver skal løses samtidig.

Vi lægger vægt på, at du:

• 
Har erfaring med koordinering, projektarbejde, administration eller produktionsplanlægning.

• 
Er god til at planlægge og holde styr på flere projekter og deadlines.

• 
Er omhyggelig og har øje for detaljerne.

• 
Tager ansvar og selv følger op på det, der mangler.

• 
Kan tilpasse dig, når planer og prioriteringer ændrer sig.

• 
Har lyst til en hverdag med forskellige opgaver og både koordinering og praktisk arbejde.

• 
Er en god kollega, der samarbejder og hjælper til.

Erfaring med video, livestreaming eller broadcast er en fordel, men ikke et krav. Det samme gælder lettere billedbehandling, videoredigering eller grundlæggende grafisk arbejde. Dansk er en fordel, men ikke et krav.

AVdesign er en international produktionsvirksomhed i Billund, grundlagt i 2005. Vi er 16 kolleger inden for blandt andet animation, filmproduktion, lyd og produktionsledelse og løser opgaver for kunder over hele verden.

Stillingen er et barselsvikariat med tiltrædelse hurtigst muligt. Arbejdsstedet er Billund, og stillingen kræver fysisk fremmøde.

jobs.occupation: Would you like to combine your engineering studies with practical experience in project management and learn how technical solutions and business priorities come together?
jobs.description:
Would you like to combine your engineering studies with practical experience in project management and learn how technical solutions and business priorities come together?

At Gram Equipment, we develop and deliver equipment for industrial ice cream production worldwide. We are looking for an engineering student to join our Project Management team in Kolding, either as an intern or a student worker.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues and gain insight into how we coordinate projects, from technical requirements and planning to delivery. Along the way, you will learn how mechanical solutions, customer expectations, budgets and deadlines influence project decisions.

What you will be doing
You will support our project managers in their daily work, with tasks adapted to your skills, interests and study requirements. Your tasks may include:

• Supporting project planning and following up on milestones, deadlines and outstanding actions.
• Preparing and updating project documentation, status reports and meeting materials.
• Participating in project meetings and following up on agreed actions.
• Helping coordinate activities across Engineering, Sales, Production, Installation and Service.
• Supporting the follow-up on project costs, changes and risks.
• Contributing ideas to improve project processes and ways of working.

As you develop your understanding of our projects, you will have the opportunity to take responsibility for defined tasks with guidance from the team.

Who we are looking for
You are studying Mechanical Engineering, Global Business Engineering or a related engineering programme. You have a good understanding of mechanical principles and an interest in the business side of engineering, particularly how technical decisions affect costs, delivery and customer value.

We also imagine that you:

• Are curious about project management and eager to apply your knowledge in practice.
• Work in a structured way and follow through on your tasks.
• Enjoy collaborating with people across different functions.
• Take initiative and ask questions when you need input.
• Communicate clearly in English, both spoken and written.
You do not need previous project management experience. What matters is your willingness to learn and contribute.

What we offer
You will gain practical experience in an international engineering company, with support and feedback from experienced project managers. You will work on real projects and develop your technical, commercial and coordination skills.

Our main office in Kolding offers an informal working environment with dedicated colleagues.

Looking for an internship? We will agree on the duration, scope and learning objectives in line with your study programme.

Looking for a student job? We will agree on working hours that fit in with your studies, with flexibility during exam periods.

Interested?

Please send your CV and a short application explaining your motivation. Let us know whether you are interested in an internship, a student job or either option, and include your preferred start date and availability.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Chip Ecosystem Partnership and Funding Manager, The position is a Senior Advisor at TEK Innovation
jobs.description:
Do you want to help facilitate and grow the semiconductor and chip ecosystem in Denmark and beyond, working with the leading researchers in the field, and to turn potential into opportunities, partnerships and projects? Then this job could be for you.  

About the position 

SDU Microelectronics at TEK, headed by professor Farshad Moradi, is part of the Danish Chips Competence Centre (DkCCC) - the new Danish hub for chip technology and your strategic platform. The position offers an opportunity to play a central role in strengthening Denmark’s chip ecosystem and to help connect the ecosystem with fast-growing application areas such as drones, robotics, sensors and autonomous systems, where advanced chip technology is becoming increasingly critical for performance, reliability, energy efficiency and future innovation. 

You will work closely with SDU researchers, DkCCC partners, Danish universities, companies, incubators, industry organizations, funding advisers and European chip networks. Learn more here www.dkccc.eu 

The position involves regular travel within Denmark and occasional travel elsewhere in Europe. 

Your main responsibilities will include:  

• 
Identifying relevant national and European funding opportunities in chip technology, semiconductor development, and chip-enabled applications. 

• 
Developing and maintaining a strategic pipeline of funding calls, project ideas and potential consortium partners. 

• 
Engaging proactively with Danish start-ups, SMEs and established companies to understand their technological needs and funding requirements. 

• 
Connecting companies with relevant researchers, facilities and competencies at SDU and other Danish universities. 

• 
Helping companies and researchers translate technical and business ideas into fundable project concepts. 

• 
Initiating and facilitating Danish and European consortia for chip-related funding calls and identifying opportunities to join existing consortia. 

• 
Promoting Danish chip competencies and contribute to the visibility and strategic development of DkCCC.  

• 
Supporting the full process of funding applications, from project objectives and facilitating consortiums, to coordinating proposals with partners and funding advisers. 

• 
Building relationships with key stakeholders, organizing activities, and events supporting the ecosystem.   

Your profile 
You have a relevant master's degree, for example within engineering or natural sciences, business development or innovation management, economics or business administration, European studies or public policy, research and innovation management, or another relevant field. 

You have documented experience in one or more of the following: 

• 
National or European research and innovation funding 

• 
Development of collaborative funding proposals 

• 
Consortium building and partner identification 

• 
University–industry collaboration or innovation/business development 

• 
Supporting start-ups, SMEs or deep-tech companies 

• 
Stakeholder management and professional networking 

We are looking for a colleague who: 

• 
Is proactive and comfortable initiating contact with companies, researchers and potential partners.  

• 
Is a strong relationship builder who can establish trust across organizational and disciplinary boundaries 

• 
Understands both commercial needs and academic interests and can structure complex consortium-development processes, while maintaining momentum towards a deadline 

• 
Communicates clearly with different stakeholders, technical, academia and experts, business 

• 
Works independently and is persistent and solution oriented, while also contributing actively to a team 

Experience with semiconductors, microelectronics, integrated circuits, quantum technologies, photonics, sensors or other deep-tech fields is a significant advantage — though you don't need to be a chip designer. What matters more is your ability to grasp technology-based opportunities, engage technical specialists, and turn complex ideas into fundable partnerships. Knowledge of European research and innovation programs, including EU Chips Act calls, is also an advantage. 

What we offer 

• 
Become part of SDU’s growing environment for microelectronics and chip technology. 

• 
Build partnerships that may lead to new products, technologies, companies, and investments. 

• 
Work directly with promising Danish start-ups, companies and research environments. 

• 
Help create new university–industry collaborations. 

• 
Develop national and European networks within a strategically important technology area. 

• 
Influence the formation of projects from their earliest stages.  

• 
Collaborate with leading researchers and industry specialists, in an international and interdisciplinary environment. 

• 
A role with considerable independence and the opportunity to shape the methods, networks, and activities used to identify funding opportunities and develop consortia. 

Your organizational home will be TEK Innovation, the research support and innovation unit at TEK, where you will have colleagues with similar jobs, supporting emerging ecosystems, as well as funding advisors and project managers. Your academic home with SDU Microelectronics, where you will work closely with professor Farshad Moradi and his team.  

For further information about the position, please contact: 

Thit Juul Hvid, Head of TEK Innovation, The Technical Faculty at The University of Southern Denmark tjuul@tek.sdu.dk 

Professor Farshad Moradi, SDU Microelectronics, The Technical faculty at The University of Southern Denmark at moradi@sdu.dk  

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support. 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST).

First Interview: week 46, second interview, week 47.

The startdate will be January 1, 2027, or at the earliest convenience.

Salary and employment terms:  

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Application must include cover letter, CV and exam certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

All documents must be in English and PDF format.  All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.  

You can only apply for the position at – https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu. 

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

Confidence in opening doors, starting conversations, and building relationships.
